Bekker's Anecdota p. 383,31: ἀλκάθω καὶ ἀλκάθειν [I help and to help]. Sophocles and Aeschylus (fr. 425), and it means βοηθεῖν [to help]. There is no present ἀλκάθω ἀλκάθειν [I help, to help], but the aorist άλκαθεῖν [to have helped]. Infinitives of this kind are usually written with an acute accent on the penult in manuscripts.
